dedupe_keys.name: kke disaster evacuation simulation solution multi agent evacuation of people hazards and structures

description: KKE, a Japanese engineering and simulation company, offers disaster evacuation simulation as a consulting solution that combines hazards, structures and people to judge measures against tsunami, earthquake and other disasters. The page explains that after the 2011 Great East Japan Earthquake, reliance on hard defences alone was seen to fail against events beyond design, and that planners now mix hard measures, such as sea walls and evacuation facilities, with soft ones such as land use rules, route signs, drills and workshops. Multi-agent simulation models each evacuee with their own traits, such as people with disabilities, older people, walking speed and route, to test whether routes, shelters and facilities work, and results are shown as animations for staff training and building consensus, including layout changes inside buildings. Coverage: projects in Japan. Access: consulting service on request. Licence: commercial. Caveats: the page gives no model documentation or validation details. Simulation uses are agent-based evacuation studies of towns, public spaces and facilities under tsunami and earthquake scenarios. Related records: the Kumamoto PLATEAU flood evacuation use case and Pathfinder.
